payload.task_text:
Hello, I need to prepare a quarterly portfolio review for our investment committee. The portfolio holds five stocks: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, and XOM. Please look up the stock price data for Q4 2025 (October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025) for each of these tickers.

For each stock, I need: the closing price on the first trading day of the quarter (start price), the closing price on the last trading day of the quarter (end price), the quarterly return as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal, the highest price during the quarter (quarter high), the lowest price during the quarter (quarter low), and the average daily trading volume.

Create a PowerPoint presentation called Portfolio_Review.pptx in the workspace with the following structure:

A title slide with "Q4 2025 Portfolio Review" as the title and "AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM" as the subtitle.

A portfolio overview slide showing which stocks are in the portfolio, the review period, the best performing stock with its return percentage, and the worst performing stock with its return percentage.

One slide for each stock (5 slides total) showing the stock symbol as the title and all the metrics listed above (start price, end price, return, quarter high, quarter low, average volume).

A final "Key Takeaways" slide summarizing the best performer, worst performer, and the average portfolio return across all five stocks rounded to 1 decimal.

Also, please schedule a calendar event for the portfolio review meeting on March 15, 2026 from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM with title "Q4 2025 Portfolio Review Meeting" and location "Conference Room A".
Note: Use the America/New_York timezone for all calendar events in this task.


Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. Five independent Q4 history calls can run natively in parallel, after which one presentation identifier is the only real write dependency.

Resolve the workspace dynamically. In one response call `get_historical_stock_prices` for `AMZN`, `GOOGL`, `JNJ`, `JPM`, and `XOM` natively in parallel with `start_date="2025-10-01"`, `end_date="2026-01-01"`, `interval="1d"`, and `auto_adjust=true` so the end-exclusive API still includes 2025-12-31. For each symbol, sort valid dated rows ascending, reject duplicates/missing closes, use first and last observed trading closes, compute return `(end/start-1)*100`, quarter high/low from the returned adjusted OHLC series, and average daily volume. Freeze one five-row table with source row counts/date bounds and derive best, worst, and simple mean return from unrounded values before display rounding.

In parallel with those reads, call `list_events` for a narrow ISO range covering March 15, 2026 with sufficient `maxResults` and `orderBy="startTime"`, then inspect exact title/time locally. If absent, call `create_event` once with summary `Q4 2025 Portfolio Review Meeting`, start/end local ISO values `2026-03-15T14:00:00`/`2026-03-15T15:00:00`, `timeZone="America/New_York"` in both objects, and location `Conference Room A`; retain its ID for `get_event`. The main agent is the sole presentation writer: create `Portfolio_Review.pptx` once, retain one presentation ID, and build exactly eight slides—title, overview, one per symbol, and Key Takeaways—with all task-requested metrics and one-decimal returns. Do not create a slide per data call or a second deck. Read back slide count, titles, and all five stock metric blocks; read back the event; reconcile best/worst/average values, complete the task, and do not dispatch a verification agent.

nodes.text:
Read-only market data task for an investment committee quarterly review. Compile Q4 2025 (US trading quarter: October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025) price metrics for five tickers: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM.

DATA FETCH
For EACH of the five tickers, call mcp__yahoo-finance__get_historical_stock_prices with:
- ticker = <TICKER>
- start_date = "2025-10-01"
- end_date = "2026-01-01"  (requested slightly past quarter end so that a possibly-exclusive end date cannot drop the Dec 31 row; only use rows dated 2025-10-01 .. 2025-12-31)
- leave interval and auto_adjust at their defaults (daily, auto-adjusted)

Fallback: if the end_date "2026-01-01" call errors, retry with end_date = "2025-12-31". If that result is missing a 2025-12-31 row, additionally call mcp__yahoo-finance__get_stock_price_by_date(ticker=<TICKER>, date="2025-12-31") to obtain the final close and note that you did so.

METRICS (computed per ticker, using ONLY rows dated 2025-10-01 through 2025-12-31 inclusive):
- start_price = Close on the first trading day of the quarter (expected 2025-10-01)
- end_price = Close on the last trading day of the quarter (expected 2025-12-31)
- return_pct = (end_price / start_price - 1) * 100. Report this UNROUNDED to 4 decimals, AND rounded to 1 decimal.
- quarter_high = maximum of daily High values in the quarter
- quarter_low = minimum of daily Low values in the quarter
- avg_volume = arithmetic mean of daily Volume values in the quarter (report to 2 decimals)

Also report per ticker: the first and last trading dates observed and the number of trading rows used, so we can confirm the window is correct. Sanity-check that start is ~Oct 1 and end is ~Dec 31; if the data starts/ends on different dates, report the actual dates and use the actual first/last trading day closes as start/end prices.

DELIVERABLE (return in your final message, no files):
For each ticker one line:
TICKER | start=<close> | end=<close> | return_unrounded=<x.xxxx> | return_pct=<x.x> | high=<max High> | low=<min Low> | avg_volume=<mean> | window=<first_date>..<last_date> | rows=<n>
Plus a one-line note on any data anomalies (missing dates, fallbacks used). Double-check the return arithmetic before reporting. Do not write any files; this is a read-only research task.
Compile Q4 2025 stock metrics

Create a PowerPoint file at EXACTLY this path (create it there, do not save anywhere else):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-yf-portfolio-ppt-gcal/workspace/Portfolio_Review.pptx

Use the mcp__pptx__ tools (create_presentation, add_slide, populate_placeholder, add_bullet_points, save_presentation, extract_presentation_text). The deck must have EXACTLY 8 slides with EXACTLY the content below. Do not add, drop, reorder, or reword anything. Slide 1 should use the title layout (layout_index=0, title + subtitle placeholders); slides 2-8 should use a title+content layout (e.g., layout_index=1) with the title placeholder = the slide title and the body placeholder = the bullets in the listed order.

SLIDE 1 (title slide)
Title: Q4 2025 Portfolio Review
Subtitle: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM

SLIDE 2
Title: Portfolio Overview
Bullets (4, in this order):
- Portfolio Stocks: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM
- Review Period: Q4 2025 (October 1, 2025 - December 31, 2025)
- Best Performer: GOOGL (27.9%)
- Worst Performer: JPM (4.2%)

SLIDE 3

Bullets (6):

- End Price: $230.82
- Quarterly Return: 4.6%
- Quarter High: $258.60
- Quarter Low: $211.03
- Average Daily Volume: 45,111,094

SLIDE 4

- Quarterly Return: 27.9%
- Quarter High: $328.62
- Quarter Low: $235.69
- Average Daily Volume: 35,360,358

SLIDE 5

SLIDE 6

SLIDE 7

Formatting rules: dollar prices with 2 decimals and thousands separators exactly as shown; percentages exactly as shown (one decimal + %); volumes as integers with comma separators, no decimals. If a bullet auto-adds a bullet character that is fine, but the text itself must match exactly.

WORKFLOW: create the presentation, add/populate all 8 slides, save_presentation to the exact path above, then VERIFY by running extract_presentation_text (or per-slide extraction) and compare against this spec. If anything is missing, wrong, or on the wrong slide, fix it and re-save before finishing.

DELIVERABLE in your final message: confirmation that the file is saved, the absolute file path, the slide count, and the per-slide extracted text (or a statement that each slide matches the spec verbatim), plus any deviations you had to make.
